Path What it is .coderagent/config.yaml The configuration of the project .coderagent/rules.yaml The permission rules of the project .coderagent/agents/*.md The sub agents of the project .coderagent/skills/*/SKILL.md The skills of the project .coderagent/plugins/*/plugin.py The plugins of the project .coderagent/commands/*.md The commands of the project .coderagent/memory/projects.md What the agent remembers about the project .coderagent/pending-memory.md The preferences that wait for a confirmation AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md The instructions of the project ~/.coderagent/config.yaml The configuration of the user ~/.coderagent/litellm_config.yaml The aliases of the models ~/.coderagent/rules.yaml The permission rules of the user ~/.coderagent/CLAUDE.md The instructions and the preferences of the user ~/.coderagent/agents/, ~/.coderagent/skills/, ~/.coderagent/plugins/ The extensions of the user ~/.coderagent/trusted-plugins.json The plugins the user trusts ~/.coderagent/sessions/ The event log of the sessions ~/.coderagent/checkpoints/ The checkpoints of the sessions

MSWEA_CODER_HOME moves the whole user directory somewhere else.

docs.title: The commands of the coding agent
docs.text:
中文版：命令

The coder command starts an interactive session. Everything that starts with a slash is a command, everything else is a message for the agent.

coder                 # the terminal interface
coder --task "fix the failing test"   # one turn, then the answer
coder --task "/help"  # a command without the interface

docs.title: The built-in commands
docs.text:
Command What it does /help The list of the commands /model (/m) Show or switch the model /mode Show or switch the permission mode /plan Switch to plan mode, where nothing is changed /compact Compact the conversation now /clear Start a new session /resume List the sessions or resume one /fork Copy the session into a new one /rewind Show the checkpoints or roll back to one /diff Show the changes in the working tree /init Write an AGENTS.md for this project /cost The tokens and the money spent /todos The task list of the agent /mcp The MCP servers and their state /permissions The rules that are in effect /hooks The hooks that are loaded /agents The sub agents that are available /skills The skills that are available /plugins The plugins, or trust one of them /memory The memory of the project and of the user /status The state of the session /sandbox Where the commands of the agent run /export Write the conversation to a file /context The size of the context /exit (/quit) Leave the interface

The money of /cost is the money of the session. A new session (/clear) starts at zero, whatever the session before it spent.

/exit closes the terminal interface, the same way ctrl+q does. In the browser there is nothing to close, so it says that the server keeps running: stop it with ctrl+c in the terminal that started it.

docs.title: Your own commands
docs.text:
A command is a markdown file in .coderagent/commands. The file starts with a front matter, the way Claude Code does it:

---
description: Generate a commit message
argument-hint: [file]
allowed-tools: bash(git diff:*), read
---
Describe the change of $1.
Everything else: $ARGUMENTS
  • $ARGUMENTS becomes everything the user typed after the command.
  • $1, $2, … become the arguments, one by one.
  • allowed-tools limits the tools the command may use. The tools of the session are back when the command is done.
  • model picks another model for this command.

Only the name of the tool is read. The part in parentheses is thrown away, so bash(git diff:*) allows the bash tool for every command it runs — there is no way to restrict a tool to a pattern. Write bash and remember that the command may run anything.

The command above is used like this:

/commit src/coderagent/core/loop.py

A file without a front matter is ignored. The commands are looked up in <cwd>/.coderagent/commands/*.md — the agent does not walk up the directories to find them.

docs.title: 命令
docs.text:
coder 命令起一个交互式会话。以斜杠开头的是命令，其余都是给 agent 的消息。

coder                 # 终端界面
coder --task "把失败的测试修好"   # 跑一轮，然后是答案
coder --task "/help"  # 不进界面，直接跑一个命令

英文版：The commands of the coding agent

docs.title: 内置命令
docs.text:
命令 干什么 /help 命令的列表 /model（/m） 看或者换模型 /mode 看或者换权限模式 /plan 切到 plan 模式，什么都不改 /compact 现在就压缩对话 /clear 开一个新会话 /resume 列出会话，或者续接一个 /fork 把会话复制成一个新会话 /rewind 列出检查点，或者退回去一个 /diff 看工作区里的改动 /init 给这个项目写一个 AGENTS.md /cost 已经花掉的 token 和钱 /todos agent 的任务清单 /mcp MCP 服务器和它们的状态 /permissions 现在生效的规则 /hooks 加载了的 hook /agents 可以用的子 agent /skills 可以用的技能 /plugins 插件，或者信任其中一个 /memory 项目的记忆和用户的记忆 /status 会话的状态 /sandbox agent 的命令在哪里跑 /export 把对话写成文件 /context 上下文有多大 /exit（/quit） 退出界面

/cost 里的钱就是会话的钱。新会话（/clear）从零开始，不管上一个会话花了 多少。

/exit 关掉终端界面，和 ctrl+q 一样。浏览器里没有东西可关，所以它会说 服务还在跑：要停掉它，得在启动它的那个终端里按 ctrl+c。

docs.title: 自己的命令
docs.text:
一个命令就是 .coderagent/commands 里的一个 markdown 文件。文件开头是 front matter，和 Claude Code 一个写法：

---
description: Generate a commit message
argument-hint: [file]
allowed-tools: bash(git diff:*), read
---
Describe the change of $1.
Everything else: $ARGUMENTS
  • $ARGUMENTS 变成用户敲在命令后面的全部内容。
  • $1、$2…… 变成参数，一个一个来。
  • allowed-tools 限定这个命令能用的工具。命令干完，session 的工具就回来了。
  • model 给这个命令换一个模型。

只读工具的名字。括号里那一段会被丢掉，所以 bash(git diff:*) 放行的是 bash 这个工具的全部命令——没有办法把一个工具限定到某个写法上。写 bash 就得 记着：这个命令能跑任何东西。

上面那个命令这么用：

/commit src/coderagent/core/loop.py

没有 front matter 的文件会被忽略。命令只在 <cwd>/.coderagent/commands/*.md 里找——agent 不会一层层往上找。

docs.title: The eval harness
docs.text:
The coding agent is a harness: an event log, a permission layer, structured tools, a context engine, a trace. A harness that is never measured is a harness that is never improved. coder eval runs a suite of tasks and reports what the agent did, so that a change of the harness can be compared with the change before it.

coder eval evals/basic --format json --out /tmp/eval.json

docs.title: The suite
docs.text:
A suite is a directory, every task is a directory inside it. A task has a task.yaml and, next to it, the files that are the initial state of the working directory of the agent.

# evals/basic/off-by-one/task.yaml
id: off-by-one                # optional, the name of the directory by default
prompt: |                     # or `prompts:`, a list of them: one turn each
  The function `add_one` in calc.py is off by one. Fix it so that the test passes.
setup:                        # optional, in the working directory, before the agent
  - pip install -e .
verify:                       # required, in the working directory, after the agent
  - python -m pytest -q tests/test_calc.py
timeout: 300                  # optional, the seconds of the agent (default 300)
verify_timeout: 300           # optional, the seconds of each verify command
expect: pass                  # optional, `pass` (default) or `fail`
tags: [bugfix]                # optional
require_tools:               # optional, the tools the task needs, and the files they touch
  - tools: [edit, multi_edit]
    paths: [calc.py]
config:                       # optional, a yaml file or `a.b=c` overrides
  - permissions.yaml          # a yaml file next to the task.yaml
  - agent.max_turns=20
script:                       # optional, the scripted model. Empty means: the real model.
  - content: Let me look at the file first.
    tool_calls:
      - tool: read
        args: {path: calc.py}
  - content: Found it. Fixing it.
    tool_calls:
      - tool: edit
        args:
          path: calc.py
          old_string: "return n + 2"
          new_string: "return n + 1"
  - content: The test passes now.

Every file of the task directory that is not a yaml file is a fixture: it is copied into the working directory before the agent starts.

prompts: gives the agent several turns, one after the other, in the same session. A task with a single prompt can never compact: the cut of the history has to land on a turn boundary, and a turn that never happened cannot be cut. A task that wants to see the compaction — and to measure the size of the summary — needs more than one prompt.

The verify commands are the judgement of the task: the task passed when all of them exit with 0. A task without a verify is refused when the suite is loaded, so a suite cannot pass by doing nothing.

expect: fail is for the tasks that must not pass: a guard that keeps the suite honest, because a check that never fails would let every task pass. The report says whether a task did what it was supposed to do (as_expected), and the summary counts the ones that did not (unexpected). A guard that failed as it should is still a failed task in the pass rate of the report: the pass rate counts what the verify commands said, the comparison is the one that leaves the guards out.

require_tools names what the task needs from the tools: one of the requirements has to be met. The result of the task alone is not enough, because an agent that rewrites the file with the shell would pass the check while the tool stayed broken. A requirement names the tools that may do the work and the files they have to touch:

require_tools:
  - tools: [edit, multi_edit]
    paths: [calc.py]

The file matters: an edit of another file is not the work of the task. A task that says this cannot be solved with the shell, so a broken edit shows up as a failed task.

A config entry may be a yaml file next to the task.yaml, so that a task brings its own settings. The tasks of evals/basic use it for their permission rules: the mode and the rules of the task win over the mode of the command, and they forbid the routes around the tool the task needs.

The script is a scripted model: the answers of the agent are written down instead of asked for. It needs no API key, so a task with a script runs offline, and it makes the trajectory of the harness itself reproducible. A task without a script runs against the real model. A suite may mix scripted and live tasks, and the report says which is which ("mode").

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
coder eval <suite> \
  [-m MODEL] [-c SPEC ...] [--only ID ...] [--tag TAG ...] \
  [--format text|json] [--out FILE] [--keep] [--label NAME] \
  [--run-dir DIR] [--permission-mode bypass|default]
  • --only and --tag select the tasks of the suite.
  • --format json prints the report as json. --out always writes the json report.
  • --run-dir keeps the working directories and the sessions in a place you choose.
  • --keep keeps the temporary directory of the run.
  • --permission-mode default asks for the approval of a human that is never there: the agent is not blocked, but the report counts the questions it would have asked (approvals).

docs.title: The report
docs.text:
{
  "format": "coder-eval-1.0",
  "label": "live-1",
  "suite": "evals/basic",
  "model": "nengpa/minimax-m2.7",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:9f2c…",
  "config": {"…": "the input of the fingerprint, as it was"},
  "started_at": 1762830000.0,
  "duration_seconds": 41.2,
  "summary": {
    "tasks": 3, "passed": 2, "failed": 1, "errors": 0, "unexpected": 0,
    "pass_rate": 0.667,
    "total_cost": 0.0412, "total_tokens_in": 12345, "total_tokens_out": 6789,
    "total_model_calls": 12, "total_tool_calls": 30,
    "compactions": 1, "summary_ratio_mean": 0.12, "summary_ratio_max": 0.12
  },
  "tasks": [
    {
      "id": "off-by-one", "mode": "live", "passed": true,
      "expect": "pass", "as_expected": true,
      "stop_reason": "end_turn", "error": "", "error_kind": "",
      "cost": 0.012, "tokens_in": 800, "tokens_out": 200,
      "model_calls": 7, "tool_calls": 9, "tool_errors": 1, "approvals": 0,
      "compactions": 1, "summary_ratios": [0.12],
      "duration_seconds": 5.1, "session_id": "20261111-a1b2c3",
      "setup": [],
      "verify": [
        {"command": "python -m pytest -q tests/test_calc.py",
         "exit_code": 0, "timed_out": false, "output": "1 passed"}
      ]
    }
  ]
}

The cost of a model that litellm does not know is 0, so the tokens are always in the report next to it: they come from the provider and they are reliable.

model_calls counts the calls of the main loop. The calls of the sub agents are not in it, their cost is.

tool_errors counts the tool calls that failed, the ones that were denied included.

summary_ratios holds one number per compaction: the size of the summary against the size of the history it replaces. A ratio that grows means the summary became verbose, or the history it summarizes became noisy. The mean and the worst of them are in the summary of the run.

docs.title: The fingerprint
docs.text:
The fingerprint is the hash of the configuration the agent ran with: the model, the system prompt, the tools, the permission mode, the context and the sandbox. Two runs with the same fingerprint are comparable, two runs with a different one are not: the configuration changed, so the numbers moved for that reason. It is a hash of the configuration and not of the code, so a change of the harness that touches nothing in the configuration leaves the fingerprint alone.

The input of the fingerprint is in the report as well, so a diff of two reports says what changed:

diff <(jq -S .tasks before.json) <(jq -S .tasks after.json)

docs.title: The isolation
docs.text:
Every task runs on its own: its own working directory, its own session, its own model. The sessions, the checkpoints, the rules and the memory of the user go to a temporary directory, so a run of the eval does not touch the data of the user nor the repository.

The file tools cannot leave the working directory, not even in the bypass mode, and neither can the bash tool: a command that names a path outside of it is refused in every mode. What a local eval does run on your machine is the command itself: a local eval runs the commands the model writes. Run it in a container, or with a sandbox type of your choice (sandbox.type in the configuration).

docs.title: The comparison
docs.text:
Two reports of the same suite say whether a change of the harness made the agent worse:

coder eval-compare after.json --against before.json

The exit code is the verdict: zero when the change is good, one when a task that used to pass does not pass any more. Only the tasks that both runs have are compared, and a task with expect: fail is not a rate but a guard.

coder eval-compare after.json \
  [--against before.json] [--max-regressions N] [--max-drop R] \
  [--same-config] [--format text|json] [--out FILE]
  • Without --against the report is only checked against what its tasks were supposed to do: a task that did not, or a task the harness could not grade, is a problem.
  • --max-regressions and --max-drop forgive a little. The real model is not deterministic, so a live suite needs a margin; a scripted suite does not.
  • With --against the margin applies to the regressions and to the fall of the rate. A task that regressed is forgiven by the margin, not reported twice. The guard of a suite and a task the harness could not grade are never forgiven.
  • --same-config says nothing when the two runs did not run the same configuration: the numbers of two different configurations say nothing about the change, so the comparison says nothing and the exit code is zero.

docs.title: The check of the pull request
docs.text:
.github/workflows/eval.yaml runs the suite of the pull request, runs it again with the harness of the base, and compares the two:

git worktree add /tmp/base <the commit of the base>
cp -r evals/offline /tmp/base/evals/
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/base/src python -c "from coderagent.ui.cli import app; app()" \
  eval /tmp/base/evals/offline --label base --format json --out base.json
coder eval-compare head.json --against base.json

The suite of the CI is evals/offline: every task of it is scripted, so the check needs no API key and says the same thing every time. It holds a task that must fail, so the check of the suite cannot be vacuous. Both runs of the comparison use that same suite; the pull request decides whether the check runs at all, by the files it touches.

The job live does the same with evals/basic and the real model. It is manual, it needs the secrets of the model, and it forgives nothing: the real model is not deterministic, so a failure of the job is a reason to run it again, not a verdict. It compares with --same-config, so a run that changed the configuration says nothing instead of blaming the change.

The two jobs are not equally sensitive. The scripted one is exact: a harness that breaks a tool fails its task, and the job says so. The live one is not: a model that meets a broken tool often finds another way, so a broken harness can cost a single task out of nine. The scripted job is the gate; the live one is the signal.

docs.title: The example suite
docs.text:
evals/basic holds nine tasks. They have no script, so they run against the real model and they need an API key:

coder eval evals/basic --label live-1 --format json --out /tmp/eval.json
task what it is off-by-one a bug in calc.py, the agent has to find it and fix it import-error a module that imports a name that does not exist rename-symbol a function that has to be renamed in the module and in its callers create-file a file that does not exist yet, the agent has to write it cli-flag a script that ignores the argument it is given config-value a value in a configuration file that has to change grep-count a question about the files of the repository, answered in a file long-conversation several turns in one session, so that the context has to be compacted no-op a task that is already done: the agent has to leave the code alone

The last one is deliberate: an agent that changes what it should not is as much a bug as an agent that changes nothing.

Five of the tasks protect the file they change: the rules of the task refuse every other way of writing it, and the task needs the edit tool to have worked on that very file. So a broken edit fails the task instead of being routed around.

Every task but no-op fails its check before the agent starts, so a task that is solved by doing nothing is a broken task. tests/coderagent/eval/test_suite.py keeps an eye on that.

evals/offline is the other suite: six tasks, all scripted, all offline. The broken-check task is the guard of the suite: its check has to fail, so a check that never fails cannot hide. The multi-turn task has three prompts: it runs a turn for each of them, in the same session.

To run a task without an API key, give it a script: the answers of the agent are written down, and the trajectory is the same every time.

docs.title: 评测（eval）
docs.text:
coding agent 本身就是一套 harness：事件溯源、权限层、结构化工具、上下文治理、可观测性。 一套从来没有被测量过的 harness，就是一套从来没有被改进过的 harness。 coder eval 跑一批任务，把 agent 干了什么报出来，这样 harness 的每一次改动都能和上一次的对比。

coder eval evals/basic --format json --out /tmp/eval.json

docs.title: 任务集（suite）
docs.text:
一个 suite 是一个目录，里面每个子目录是一个任务。任务目录里有 task.yaml， 其余文件（除 *.yaml/*.yml 外）是 fixture：agent 开始前会被复制进工作目录。

# evals/basic/off-by-one/task.yaml
id: off-by-one                # 可选，默认取目录名
prompt: |                     # 或者 `prompts:`，一个列表：每个 prompt 一轮
  calc.py 里的 add_one 差一。修好它，让测试通过。
setup:                        # 可选，在 agent 开始前于工作目录执行
  - pip install -e .
verify:                       # 必填，在 agent 结束后执行；全部 exit 0 才算通过
  - python -m pytest -q tests/test_calc.py
timeout: 300                  # 可选，agent 这一轮的墙钟秒数（默认 300）
verify_timeout: 300           # 可选，每条 verify 命令的秒数（默认 300）
expect: pass                  # 可选，`pass`（默认）或 `fail`
tags: [bugfix]                # 可选
require_tools:               # 可选，这个任务需要的工具，以及它们必须改的文件
  - tools: [edit, multi_edit]
    paths: [calc.py]
config:                       # 可选，配置覆盖：YAML 文件路径或 `a.b=c`
  - permissions.yaml          # task.yaml 旁边的 YAML 文件
  - agent.max_turns=20
script:                       # 可选，脚本化模型；为空 = 用真实模型
  - content: 先看一下文件。
    tool_calls:
      - tool: read
        args: {path: calc.py}
  - content: 找到 bug 了，改掉。
    tool_calls:
      - tool: edit
        args:
          path: calc.py
          old_string: "return n + 2"
          new_string: "return n + 1"
  - content: 改好了，测试通过。

verify 就是这个任务的判据：全部命令 exit 0 才算通过。 没有 verify 的任务在加载 suite 时就被拒绝，所以一个 suite 不可能靠「什么都不做」通过。

prompts: 给 agent 多轮：同一个会话里一个接一个。只有一个 prompt 的任务永远不会压缩—— 切点必须落在轮边界上，没发生过的轮切不了。想看到压缩、想量摘要多大，任务就得有第二个 prompt。

expect: fail 是给那些必须不通过的任务用的：它是 suite 的保险丝—— 一个从来不失败的判据，会让每个任务都通过。 报告里每个任务带 as_expected（它有没有做到该做的），summary 里数了 unexpected（没做到的有几个）。 保险丝按该有的样子失败了，在报告的通过率里仍然算一个失败任务： 通过率数的是 verify 命令说了什么，把保险丝排除在外的是对比那一步。

require_tools 写这个任务对工具的要求：这些要求里有一条要满足。 光看任务的结果是不够的：agent 用 shell 把文件重写一遍，照样能让检查通过， 而工具还是坏的。一条要求写清楚「哪些工具可以动手」和「它们必须动哪些文件」：

require_tools:
  - tools: [edit, multi_edit]
    paths: [calc.py]

文件这一项是要紧的：改了另一个文件，不算做了这个任务。 写了这条要求的任务没法用 shell 绕过去，所以 edit 一坏，任务就会失败。

config 里可以写 task.yaml 旁边的 YAML 文件，这样一个任务能自带配置。 evals/basic 的任务用它带自己的权限规则：任务的模式和规则盖过命令行的模式， 并且把「绕开这个任务需要的工具」的路都堵上。

script 是脚本化模型：agent 的回答是写死的，不是问模型要来的。 它不需要 API key，所以带 script 的任务可以离线跑，而且 harness 自己的轨迹是可复现的； 不带 script 的任务走真实模型。 一个 suite 可以混着放脚本任务和真实模型任务，报告里每个任务都带 mode。

docs.title: 命令
docs.text:
coder eval <suite> \
  [-m MODEL] [-c SPEC ...] [--only ID ...] [--tag TAG ...] \
  [--format text|json] [--out FILE] [--keep] [--label NAME] \
  [--run-dir DIR] [--permission-mode bypass|default]
  • --only 和 --tag 用来挑任务。
  • --format json 把报告打成 json；--out 写的永远是 json 报告。
  • --run-dir 把工作目录和会话留在指定的地方，--keep 保留这次运行的临时目录。
  • --permission-mode default 会去问一个并不存在的人：agent 不会被卡住， 但报告里会多一个 approvals——「本该由人介入多少次」。

docs.title: 报告
docs.text:
{
  "format": "coder-eval-1.0",
  "label": "live-1",
  "suite": "evals/basic",
  "model": "nengpa/minimax-m2.7",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:9f2c…",
  "config": {"…": "fingerprint 的输入原样"},
  "started_at": 1762830000.0,
  "duration_seconds": 41.2,
  "summary": {
    "tasks": 3, "passed": 2, "failed": 1, "errors": 0, "unexpected": 0,
    "pass_rate": 0.667,
    "total_cost": 0.0412, "total_tokens_in": 12345, "total_tokens_out": 6789,
    "total_model_calls": 12, "total_tool_calls": 30,
    "compactions": 1, "summary_ratio_mean": 0.12, "summary_ratio_max": 0.12
  },
  "tasks": [
    {
      "id": "off-by-one", "mode": "live", "passed": true,
      "expect": "pass", "as_expected": true,
      "stop_reason": "end_turn", "error": "", "error_kind": "",
      "cost": 0.012, "tokens_in": 800, "tokens_out": 200,
      "model_calls": 7, "tool_calls": 9, "tool_errors": 1, "approvals": 0,
      "compactions": 1, "summary_ratios": [0.12],
      "duration_seconds": 5.1, "session_id": "20261111-a1b2c3",
      "setup": [],
      "verify": [
        {"command": "python -m pytest -q tests/test_calc.py",
         "exit_code": 0, "timed_out": false, "output": "1 passed"}
      ]
    }
  ]
}

litellm 的价格表里没有的模型，成本恒为 0，所以 token 一定要和成本一起报： token 来自 provider，是可靠的。

model_calls 只数主循环的调用；子 agent 的调用不在里面，它们的成本在。

tool_errors 数失败的工具调用，被权限拒绝的也算。

summary_ratios 每次压缩给一个数：摘要多大，对着它替换掉的那段历史多大。 这个比值突然变大，要么是摘要变啰嗦了，要么是原文变啰嗦了。均值和最差值在整轮运行的 summary 里。

docs.title: fingerprint
docs.text:
fingerprint 是这次运行所用配置的哈希：模型、system prompt、工具、权限模式、上下文、沙箱。 两次运行 fingerprint 相同才可比；不同，说明配置变了，数字自然不一样。 它哈希的是配置而不是代码，所以只改了代码、没改配置的 harness 改动，fingerprint 不变。

fingerprint 的输入也原样放在报告里，所以两份报告一 diff，就能看出是哪一项变了：

diff <(jq -S .tasks before.json) <(jq -S .tasks after.json)

docs.title: 隔离
docs.text:
每个任务都跑在自己的地盘上：自己的工作目录、自己的会话、自己的模型。 会话、checkpoint、规则、用户记忆都被重定向到临时目录， 所以跑一次 eval 不会碰用户的数据，也不会碰仓库。

文件类工具出不了工作目录，bypass 模式也不行；bash 也一样： 命令里写了工作目录以外的路径，任何模式下都被拒。 但本地跑 eval，模型写的命令就在你的机器上执行。 请在容器里跑，或者在配置里换一个 sandbox.type。

docs.title: 对比
docs.text:
两份同一个 suite 的报告能回答「这次改 harness 到底有没有把 agent 改差」：

coder eval-compare after.json --against before.json

退出码就是结论：零 = 这次改动是好的；一 = 有任务原来能过、现在过不了了。 只比较两份报告都有的任务；expect: fail 的任务不算通过率，它只是保险丝。

coder eval-compare after.json \
  [--against before.json] [--max-regressions N] [--max-drop R] \
  [--same-config] [--format text|json] [--out FILE]
  • 不给 --against 时，只检查这份报告本身：任务没做到该做的、或者 harness 没能评判它，都是问题。
  • --max-regressions 和 --max-drop 是「原谅一点」的额度。 真实模型不是确定性的，所以 live suite 需要留点余量；脚本 suite 不需要。
  • 给了 --against 时，额度只管回归和通过率的下降：被额度原谅的回归不会再报一遍。 但保险丝被打破（expect: fail 的任务通过了）和 harness 评判不了的任务，任何额度都不原谅。
  • --same-config 在两次运行配置不同的时候什么都不说： 两份不同配置的数字说明不了这次改动，对比于是闭嘴，退出码是零。

docs.title: 拉取请求的检查
docs.text:
.github/workflows/eval.yaml 会跑一遍这个 PR 的 suite，再用基线的 harness 跑一遍，然后对比：

git worktree add /tmp/base <基线那个 commit>
cp -r evals/offline /tmp/base/evals/
PYTHONPATH=/tmp/base/src python -c "from coderagent.ui.cli import app; app()" \
  eval /tmp/base/evals/offline --label base --format json --out base.json
coder eval-compare head.json --against base.json

CI 跑的是 evals/offline：每个任务都是脚本化的，所以这个检查不需要 API key， 而且每次说的都是同一件事。它里面还有一个必须不通过的任务， 所以「判据从来不失败」这种坏情况藏不住。 对比的两次跑都用这同一个 suite；这个 PR 决定这个检查要不要跑，看它动了哪些文件。

live 这个 job 拿 evals/basic 和真实模型做同样的事。它只能手动触发， 需要模型的密钥，而且什么都不原谅：模型不是确定性的， 所以这个 job 失败是「再跑一遍」的理由，不是结论。 它用 --same-config 来对比，所以改了配置的那次跑什么都不说，而不是把账算在这次改动上。

两个 job 的灵敏度不一样。脚本那个是精确的：harness 弄坏一个工具， 对应的任务就会失败，job 会说出来。live 那个不是：模型碰到坏掉的工具 常常会绕道走，所以一个坏掉的 harness 可能只让九个任务里的一个失败。 脚本那个是闸门，live 那个是信号。

docs.title: 样例任务集
docs.text:
evals/basic 里有九个任务。它们都没有 script，所以跑的是真实模型，需要 API key：

coder eval evals/basic --label live-1 --format json --out /tmp/eval.json
任务 内容 off-by-one calc.py 里的 bug，agent 得自己找出来并修好 import-error 模块 import 了一个不存在的名字 rename-symbol 一个函数，模块里和调用它的地方都得改名 create-file 一个还不存在的文件，agent 得把它写出来 cli-flag 脚本无视了传进来的参数 config-value 配置文件里的一个值要改 grep-count 问仓库里的文件，然后把这个答案写进文件 long-conversation 一个会话里的好几轮，所以上下文得被压缩 no-op 一个已经做好的任务：agent 得什么都别改

最后一个是刻意的：不该改的时候乱改，和该改的时候不改，是同一种 bug。

九个任务里有五个把要改的文件「保护」起来：任务自己的规则挡住其它所有写法， 而且任务要求 edit 工具在这个文件上成功用过。 所以 edit 一坏，任务就失败，而不是被绕过去。

除了 no-op，每个任务在 agent 开始之前都是没通过的——一个什么都不做就能过的任务是个坏任务。 tests/coderagent/eval/test_suite.py 盯着这件事。

evals/offline 是另一个 suite：六个任务，全是脚本化的，全离线。 broken-check 是这个 suite 的保险丝：它的判据必须失败， 所以一个从来不失败的判据藏不住。multi-turn 有三个 prompt：每个 prompt 一轮，同一个会话。

想不花 API key 就跑一个任务，给它加一段 script：agent 的回答是写死的，轨迹每次都一样。

docs.title: The trace of a session
docs.text:
Every session is written to an event log, and that log is the source of truth. The export command turns it into a trace, with the metrics of the session.

coder export --session 20261106-a1b2c3 --format json --out trace.json
coder export --session 20261106-a1b2c3 --format otel --out trace.otlp
coder export --cwd .                       # the newest session of this directory

Without --out the trace goes to the standard output.

docs.title: The json format
docs.text:
The format is coder-agent-1.0, next to the mini-swe-agent-1.1 of mini-swe-agent:

{
  "trajectory_format": "coder-agent-1.0",
  "session": {
    "id": "20261106-a1b2c3",
    "cwd": "/home/me/project",
    "created_at": 1762310400.0,
    "updated_at": 1762310900.0,
    "state": "done",
    "model_name": "deepseek/deepseek-flash",
    "permission_mode": "default",
    "turn_count": 3,
    "total_cost": 0.42
  },
  "events": [
    {
      "session_id": "20261106-a1b2c3",
      "type": "user_message",
      "timestamp": 1762310400.0,
      "payload": {"content": "fix the test"}
    }
  ],
  "metrics": {
    "total_cost": 0.42,
    "total_tokens_in": 120433,
    "total_tokens_out": 8421,
    "model_calls": 9,
    "tool_calls": 60,
    "per_tool": {"read": 42, "bash": 13, "edit": 5},
    "per_purpose_cost": {"main": 0.38, "cheap": 0.04},
    "per_model_cost": {"deepseek/deepseek-flash": 0.38},
    "duration_seconds": 412.3,
    "compactions": 3,
    "summary_ratios": [0.06, 0.07, 0.05],
    "errors": 0
  }
}

summary_ratios holds one number per compaction: how much of the compacted history the summary kept. It is the gauge of the quality of the summary.

docs.title: The otel format
docs.text:
The same session as OTLP/JSON: one span per turn, one span per tool call. The file goes into Jaeger, Tempo or any other place that reads OTLP.

{
  "resourceSpans": [
    {
      "resource": {"attributes": [{"key": "session.id", "value": {"stringValue": "20261106-a1b2c3"}}]},
      "scopeSpans": [
        {
          "scope": {"name": "coderagent"},
          "spans": [
            {
              "name": "turn",
              "spans": [{"name": "tool.read", "parentSpanId": "..."}]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Where the money went
docs.text:
The /cost command shows the same metrics, with the cost of the session split by purpose, by model and by tool:

model: deepseek/deepseek-flash
calls: 9
tokens in the context: 120433
tokens spent: 128854
cost so far: $0.4200
cost: $0.4200
tokens: 120433 in, 8421 out
model calls: 9
tool calls: 60
duration: 412.3s
by purpose:
  main        $0.3800
  cheap       $0.0400
by model:
  deepseek/deepseek-flash  $0.4200
by tool:
  bash         13
  edit          5
  read         42

The purpose is the job the model was called for: main for the agent itself, the purpose of the sub agent for a delegated task, summarize for the summary of a compacted context and reflect for the memory of the session.

docs.title: The features of the coding agent
docs.text:
A list of everything coder can do, one line per feature, with an example and the errors of every part. The pages that describe a part in detail are linked at the end of each section.

中文版：coding agent 的功能

docs.title: The ways to run it
docs.text:
• One turn from the terminal — coder -t "fix the failing test". The answer is printed as text, or as JSON with --output-format json.
  • The terminal interface — coder without a task, or coder --tui. A full screen interface with a status bar, tool cards and approvals.
  • The browser — coder web. The same agent in a chat page, with a settings page for the model.
  • As an API — every action of the browser is a plain HTTP call, so a script can drive the agent.
  • As a library — coderagent.run.run_turn and build_loop put the agent into another Python program.
  • In a benchmark — the run scripts of mini-swe-agent solve SWE-bench and ProgramBench with the same model interface.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# One turn, the answer as text.
coder -t "add a docstring to src/app.py"

# One turn, the answer as JSON (for a script).
coder -t "list the files of this directory" --output-format json

# The terminal interface.
coder                      # with a terminal this is the TUI
coder --tui                # the same, said explicitly

# The browser.
coder web --cwd . --port 8765

# A session of this directory, the newest first.
coder --list

The JSON of one turn has the fields session_id, messages, cost, session_cost, stop_reason and error:

{
  "session_id": "20261109-3f0a91",
  "messages": [{"role": "assistant", "content": "I added the docstring."}],
  "cost": 0.0012,
  "session_cost": 0.0143,
  "stop_reason": "end_turn",
  "error": ""
}

cost is what the turn cost, session_cost what the whole session has cost so far.

stop_reason is one of end_turn, max_turns, cost_exceeded, token_limit, verify_failed, error and interrupted.

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text:
What you see What it means What to do no task given No -t, no --tui, and stdin is not a terminal (a script, a pipe). Give a task: coder -t "...". session 20261109-3f0a91 The same as above, but a session was found to continue. Same; add -t to run a turn in it. Unknown command '/foo'. Try /help. The line started with / but no command has that name. Check the spelling, or /help for the list. ValueError: 'bogus' is not a valid PermissionMode --permission-mode bogus — the flag is checked when the policy is built, and the exception is not caught. Use one of default, acceptEdits, plan, readonly, bypass. ValueError: Unknown output format: xml --output-format accepts only text and json. Use text or json. Unknown format 'xml'. Use json or otel. coder export --format accepts only json and otel. Use json or otel. no sessions yet --list found no session in this directory. Nothing to do; run a turn first. coder web: cannot listen on 127.0.0.1:8765 (Address already in use). on stderr, exit code 1 The port is taken. The server checks this itself before it starts, because uvicorn's own error does not say what to do. Use another port: coder web --port 8766.

coder exits with 0 after a normal turn, whatever the answer was, and with 1 when it could not start at all (a bad flag value, a port that is taken).

docs.title: The models
docs.text:
• Any provider litellm knows — OpenAI, DeepSeek, Anthropic, Gemini, Mistral, OpenRouter, … The provider in front of the name says who is called: deepseek/deepseek-flash.
  • Third party endpoints — an OpenAI compatible address in api_base, with its own key. The address may be pasted with the /chat/completions at the end; the part behind /v1 is cut off, because litellm adds it itself.
  • Aliases — a litellm config file with a model list. The model name can then be an alias of that list, and the key of the endpoint stays in the file.
  • Cache control — set_cache_control: default_end for the providers that support it. Any other value is refused.
  • Retries — max_retries, three by default.
  • Routing by purpose — a different model for main, cheap, summarize, reflect and strong.
  • Routing by the state of the session — a rule like tokens > 50000 switches to another model, and the reason is in the event log.
  • A separate model for the summary — context.summarize_model, empty means the model of the agent.
  • Streaming — the answer arrives piece by piece, in the terminal and in the browser.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# The provider is the part in front of the slash.
coder -t "..." -m deepseek/deepseek-flash

# A third party endpoint that speaks the OpenAI protocol.
coder -t "..." -m openai/MiniMax-M2.7 \
  -c model.model_kwargs.api_base=https://api.example.com/v1 \
  -c model.model_kwargs.api_key=sk-...

# .coderagent/config.yaml
model:
  model_name: deepseek/deepseek-flash
  set_cache_control: default_end
  routing:
    main: deepseek/deepseek-chat
    cheap: deepseek/deepseek-flash
    summarize: deepseek/deepseek-flash
  routing_rules:
    - when: "tokens > 50000"
      purpose: strong

The model of a turn is decided in this order:

  1. the model the user picked with /model (it wins over everything),
  2. the first routing_rules entry whose condition holds,
  3. the automatic policy: the budget is nearly used up → cheap, the context is big (> 50000 tokens) or the session is long (> 30 turns) → strong,
  4. routing.main, and without it the model of the agent.

When the model changes, the event log says why:

Switched from deepseek/deepseek-flash to deepseek/deepseek-chat: the context has grown

The reasons are the budget is nearly used up, the context has grown, the session has many turns, the rule '<when>' holds and the rules of the routing say so.

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text:
What you see What it means What to do LLM Provider NOT provided The model name has no provider in front of it. Write openai/<name> for an OpenAI compatible endpoint, or deepseek/<name>. ValueError: Invalid mode: {mode} set_cache_control is neither default_end nor empty. Use default_end, or remove the line. the file does not exist model.litellm_config points at a file that is not there. Fix the path; it is relative to the working directory. the file is not valid YAML: {error} The alias file cannot be parsed. Fix the YAML. the file has no model_list The alias file has no model_list. Add the list of the models with their litellm_params. '{name}' is not one of the aliases of this file The model name is not in the model_list of the alias file. Use one of the aliases, or drop litellm_config. BadRequestError The provider refused the request (a wrong key, a wrong name, a wrong parameter). It is not retried; the message of the provider is the answer. AuthenticationError The key is missing or wrong. Set model.model_kwargs.api_key, or the key of the endpoint in the alias file, or the key of the provider in the environment (OPENAI_API_KEY for openai/…). ContextWindowExceededError The request was larger than the window of the model. Lower context.context_window, or use a model with a bigger window.

Retries are a separate thing from the errors above: a rate limit or a timeout is retried, a bad request is not. The number of attempts comes from MSWEA_MODEL_RETRY_STOP_AFTER_ATTEMPT and is 10 by default. coder web sets that variable from model.max_retries (3 by default), so in the browser the number of attempts follows the configuration, while in the terminal it does not.

docs.title: The tools
docs.text:
The thirteen built-in tools:

Tool What it does read Read a file, with the line numbers write Write a file, creating it if needed edit Replace one exact string in a file multi_edit Several edits in one file — all of them, or none glob Find files by pattern (* in one segment, ** across directories) grep Search the contents with a regular expression, by lines, by file or by count ls List a directory; depth: -1 walks the whole tree bash Run a shell command, with a timeout or in the background bash_output The output of a background command so far bash_kill Kill a background command todo_write The task list of the current work task Hand a self contained job to a sub agent skill Load the instructions of a skill
  • Tools of MCP servers — mcp__<server>__<tool>, from every server that is configured.
  • Tools of plugins — a plugin can add tools, commands and hooks.
  • The schemas are trimmed to the budget — the schemas of the tools may take a tenth of the context window; tools.schema_budget_tokens sets another budget. When they do not fit, the ones that matter least go first. bash and read are never dropped.
  • The tool set is configurable — tools.enabled is the list of the tools the model may call, tools.disabled takes single ones away.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# The model calls these, but you can call them yourself to try them out.

{"tool": "read", "params": {"path": "src/app.py"}}
{"tool": "edit", "params": {"path": "src/app.py", "old_string": "x = 1", "new_string": "x = 2"}}
{"tool": "grep", "params": {"pattern": "def main", "output_mode": "files_with_matches"}}
{"tool": "glob", "params": {"pattern": "src/**/*.py"}}
{"tool": "ls", "params": {"path": "src", "depth": -1}}
{"tool": "bash", "params": {"command": "pytest -q", "timeout": 300}}
{"tool": "bash", "params": {"command": "pytest -q", "run_in_background": true}}
{"tool": "bash_output", "params": {"task_id": "b7f3"}}

multi_edit takes a list and is all or nothing:

{"tool": "multi_edit", "params": {"path": "src/app.py", "edits": [
  {"old_string": "import os", "new_string": "import os\nimport sys"},
  {"old_string": "def main():", "new_string": "def main(argv=None):"}
]}}

grep has three modes: content (the default), files_with_matches and count. It returns at most 100 matches, glob at most 200 files.

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text:
Every tool answers with an Error: ... line instead of raising, so the model sees the message and can correct itself. The messages are:

Tool Message read Error: file not found: {path}. Use \ls` to see what is in that directory.` read Error: '{name}' is a directory. Use \ls` to list it.` read Error: '{name}' is a binary file. edit Error: old_string not found in {path}. Use \read` to see the exact content, then retry with more context.` edit Error: old_string is not unique in {path}: it appears {count} times (lines {...}). Include more surrounding context to make it unique, or set replace_all=true. multi_edit Error: Edit #1 failed, no changes were written. {inner} — the file is untouched. grep Error: invalid regular expression '{pattern}': {error} grep Error: \output_mode` must be one of content, files_with_matches, count (got '{mode}').` glob/grep/ls Error: path not found: {path}. / Error: not a directory: {path}. bash Error: \command` is required and must be a non-empty string.` bash_output Error: unknown task id '{id}'. todo_write Error: todo #1 has invalid status '{status}'. Use one of pending, in_progress, completed. task Error: unknown sub agent '{name}'. Available sub agents: {...}. skill Error: unknown skill '{name}'. Available skills: {...}.

The errors of the executor itself are raised inside the result of the call:

Message Meaning Error: unknown tool '{name}'. Available tools: {...}. The model called a tool that is not registered — usually because tools.enabled was narrowed. Error: permission denied for '{tool}'. {reason} A rule or a mode refused the call. Error: the user denied '{tool}'. Somebody pressed n at the approval. Error: '{tool}' needs approval but no approver is available. Run with --permission-mode bypass to allow it. A call that needed approval in a headless run. --permission-mode bypass or a rule that allows it. Error: the hook blocked '{tool}'. {reason} A PreToolUse hook refused the call. Error: '{tool}' failed: {type}: {e} The tool itself raised.

A bash call that ends with a non-zero exit code is not an error: the exit code is part of the output, as [exit code 1]. A command that runs longer than tools.bash_timeout (120 seconds by default) fails with:

An error occurred while executing the command: Command 'sleep 60' timed out after 120 seconds

A background command answers with Started background task {id}: {cmd} and is read with bash_output, killed with bash_kill.

The output of a tool is written to the log of the session and sent to the provider. What looks like a secret in it — an API key, a token, a password, a private key — is replaced with [redacted] before either happens. A file that holds a secret is stored in a checkpoint without it, and it is not restored by /rewind: the file is left as it is and the command says which one it was.

docs.title: The permissions
docs.text:
• Five modes — default, acceptEdits, plan, readonly and bypass.
  • The model is told — in plan and readonly the agent knows that it may not change anything, and answers with what it found instead.
  • The shell has boundaries — the commands that only look around go through, the ones that destroy something or send it out ask, and a path outside the working directory is refused.
  • Rules — ~/.coderagent/rules.yaml and .coderagent/rules.yaml decide per tool and per pattern. The user level file wins.
  • Always allow — the button of an approval writes a rule, so the same call — the same file, or the same command — goes through from then on.
  • Denied paths — permissions.deny_paths, paths the agent may not touch.
  • Extra directories — permissions.include_dirs, directories outside the working directory the agent may still touch.
  • Three answers — allow, deny, always allow. Nobody answers, the call is denied: in the browser after ui.approval_timeout seconds (five minutes by default), in the terminal after no limit at all, because somebody is there.
  • In the terminal the answer is picked with the arrow keys, in the browser with the buttons of the card. Without a terminal the answer is a denial.
  • Hooks run before the permission check — a hook may rewrite the call or block it, and then the permission check sees the rewritten call.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
The mode decides what happens without any rule:

Mode read, glob, grep, ls write, edit, multi_edit bash todo_write, bash_output, bash_kill default allow ask ask¹ allow acceptEdits allow allow ask¹ allow plan allow deny deny allow readonly allow deny deny allow bypass allow allow allow allow

¹ The commands that only look around — ls, cat, grep, git status and the like — go through without a question. The rest asks. See the shell below.

A rule file decides per tool and per pattern:

# ~/.coderagent/rules.yaml
rules:
  - tool: bash
    pattern: "pytest"
    decision: allow
    reason: the test suite is safe to run
  - tool: edit
    pattern: "src/**/*.py"
    decision: allow
  - tool: "*"
    pattern: "*"
    decision: ask

pattern is a glob for the path tools (* in one segment, ** across directories), a regular expression for bash, and the tool name for everything else. For bash the pattern is matched against the beginning of each part of the command: git push matches git push origin main, and it does not match echo "git push".

coder -t "run the tests" --permission-mode acceptEdits
coder -t "how would you fix this?" --permission-mode plan

plan and readonly put a note into the messages the model sees:

<permission_mode mode="plan">
You are in plan mode. You may only look around: `read`, `glob`, `grep` and `ls`
work, but every tool that changes something, `bash` included, is refused.
Investigate the task and answer with the plan you would follow. The user
decides whether it is executed.
</permission_mode>

Always allow at an approval writes a rule into ~/.coderagent/rules.yaml:

rules:
  - tool: bash
    pattern: pytest
    decision: allow
    reason: always allowed by the user

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text:
What you see What it means What to do Error: permission denied for 'write'. '{path}' is outside the working directory {cwd} The agent tried to touch a path outside the working directory. Add the directory to permissions.include_dirs, or change the working directory. Error: the user denied 'write'. Somebody refused the approval. Allow it, or write a rule for it. Error: 'write' needs approval but no approver is available. Run with --permission-mode bypass to allow it. The run had no terminal (a script or a CI job) and the tool needed approval. --permission-mode bypass, or a rule with decision: allow. {path}:{line}: invalid decision '{d}', expected one of allow, ask, deny The rule file has a wrong decision. Use allow, ask or deny. {path}:{line}: unknown rule keys: {keys} The rule has a key that does not exist. The keys are tool, pattern, decision and reason. {path}: invalid YAML: {error} The rule file cannot be parsed. Fix the YAML; the message has the line. {path}: \rules` must be a list| Therules` key is not a list. Make it a list of mappings. Error: permission denied for 'bash'. '{path}' is outside the working directory {cwd} The command names a path outside the working directory. Use a path inside it, or open the directory with permissions.include_dirs.

A rule with decision: allow does not open the disk: a path outside the working directory stays outside, unless it is in permissions.include_dirs. The rules of the user cannot widen the bounds.

permissions.deny_paths adds a rule that denies everything that matches, and it is applied after the rule files, so it wins over an allow of the same path.

docs.title: The shell
docs.text:
The bash tool is the one that can do anything, so it has three boundaries.

The commands that only look around go through. ls, cat, head, tail, grep, diff, wc, jq and the reading commands of git (status, diff, log, show, …) are safe: they do not change anything and they do not reach the network. They do not ask.

The commands that destroy something or send it out ask. rm, mv, cp, chmod, curl, wget, ssh, pip, npm, docker, git push and the like. They are not refused — a person decides, and the approval says what the command does ("sends data out of the machine"). In bypass they go through like everything else, because nobody is there to ask.

A path outside the working directory is refused. cat /etc/passwd, cat ../secret, cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa and cd .. are denied in every mode, like the paths of the file tools. The programs of the system may be named (/bin/ls), the data may not leave the working directory. permissions.include_dirs opens a directory outside it.

Every part of a command is judged on its own, and the strictest part wins: an allowed pytest does not carry a rm along with it.

ls -la                       # goes through
git status                   # goes through
curl http://example.com      # asks: sends data out of the machine
pytest -q && rm -rf build    # asks: the rm is dangerous
cat /etc/passwd              # refused

docs.title: The sessions
docs.text:
• New, listed, continued, copied — --resume, --continue, --fork and --list.
  • The event log is the truth — every message, tool call, result and cost is appended to a JSONL file. A session is rebuilt by replaying it.
  • Checkpoints — a snapshot of the file before every write. /rewind rolls back to one.
  • /clear — starts a new session and keeps the old one in the log.
  • The money — tokens and cost per session, in the status bar, in /cost and in the trace.
  • The trace — coder export --format json|otel writes the session out, for a dashboard or for OpenTelemetry.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
coder -t "first task"                     # a new session
coder --list                              # the sessions of this directory
coder --resume 20261109-3f0a91 -t "more"  # continue that one
coder --continue -t "more"                # continue the newest of this directory
coder --fork 20261109-3f0a91 -t "other"   # a copy, the original stays

The files of a session live in ~/.coderagent/:

~/.coderagent/sessions/20261109-3f0a91.jsonl        # the event log
~/.coderagent/sessions/20261109-3f0a91.meta.json    # id, cwd, created_at, model_name
~/.coderagent/checkpoints/20261109-3f0a91.json       # the snapshots of the writes

The event log is one JSON object per line, and the types are user_message, assistant_message, tool_call, tool_result, approval_request, approval_response, state_change, compaction, reflection, verify, reverted_to, error and turn_end.

/rewind restores the files only — what a command did to the outside world stays done — and truncates the history of the session to the moment of the snapshot.

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text:
What you see What it means What to do ValueError: no checkpoint '<id>' in this session /rewind was given an id that is not a checkpoint of this session. /rewind without an id lists the checkpoints. /resume <unknown id> starts a session with the directory . A session id that is not in the log does not fail — it makes an empty session. Check the ids with coder --list. A turn ends with stop_reason: max_turns The agent made 50 model calls (agent.max_turns) without finishing. Raise agent.max_turns, or make the task smaller. A turn ends with stop_reason: cost_exceeded The turn cost more than agent.cost_limit. 0 means no limit. Raise agent.cost_limit. A turn ends with stop_reason: token_limit The turn used more tokens than agent.token_limit. 0 means no limit. This is the budget of a model that has no price, where the money never moves. Raise agent.token_limit. A turn ends with stop_reason: error The model call failed after the retries. The text of the error is in error. Look at error; it is the message of the provider. A turn ends with stop_reason: interrupted Somebody pressed ctrl+c. The session is saved; continue it with --resume.

A turn that ended with cost_exceeded or error is not reflected on: the memory of the session keeps what was learned before the failure.

docs.title: The context
docs.text:
• The tokens are counted — with tiktoken when it is installed, otherwise an estimate.
  • The window follows the model — 64k for DeepSeek, 200k for Claude, 128k for GPT, and so on. A configured context_window wins over the table.
  • Automatic compression — when the conversation reaches 80 % of the window, it is summarized and the history is shortened. The summary is a structure: goal, findings, decisions, files touched, open questions, next steps, errors seen.
  • What is kept — the last turns, or the last 40 % of the tokens, whichever is more.
  • /compact — compress on demand.
  • The order of the messages — system prompt, the instruction files, the todo list, the summary of the session, then the history.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
context:
  context_window: 64000
  compact_threshold: 0.8
  keep_recent_turns: 20
  keep_recent_token_ratio: 0.4
  compact_every_turns: 40
  summarize_model: deepseek/deepseek-flash

Without context_window in the configuration the window follows the name of the model: gpt- 128k, claude 200k, deepseek 64k, qwen 32k, llama 8k, gemini 1M, mistral 32k, kimi 256k, minimax 200k, and 200k for everything else.

The summary is a JSON object with these keys:

{
  "goal": "fix the failing test in test_api.py",
  "findings": ["the timeout of the client is 5 seconds, the test needs 10"],
  "decisions": ["raise the timeout in the fixture"],
  "files_touched": ["tests/test_api.py"],
  "open_questions": [],
  "next_steps": ["run the suite again"],
  "errors_seen": ["TimeoutError after 5 seconds"]
}

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text:
What you see What it means What to do ... (nothing left to compact) The turn failed because the context was too big and there was nothing left to shorten. Raise context.context_window, lower context.reserved_output, or /clear and start over. The summary is a fallback instead of the real thing The model answered with something that is not the JSON of the summary. It is tried twice, and the second time a conservative summary is used: the last five messages, with next_steps: ["re-read the files that were mentioned to recover the details"]. Nothing to do — the session continues. Ask the model again for the details it lost. recent_errors is empty although the session had errors Only the tool messages that start with Error: are collected, and only the last three of them. Nothing to do.

The token count is exact with tiktoken and an estimate without it: int(chars / 3.6) + 4 * len(messages). An estimate that is too small delays the compression, so installing tiktoken is worth it for a long session.

docs.title: The memory
docs.text:
• The memory of the project — .coderagent/memory, written at the end of a turn with what was learned about the project.
  • The memory of the user — ~/.coderagent/CLAUDE.md, with the preferences of the user.
  • Preferences wait for a confirmation — they land in pending-memory.md first, and /memory confirm writes them.
  • The instruction files — AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md of the project, and the CLAUDE.md of the user, are read by the agent.
  • It can be switched off — memory.enabled.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
The three files:

.coderagent/memory/projects.md        # what the agent learned about the project
.coderagent/pending-memory.md         # the preferences, waiting for a confirmation
~/.coderagent/CLAUDE.md                # the preferences that were confirmed

At the end of a turn the agent looks at the last 40 messages and writes what it found:

# Project memory

- the tests of the API are run with `pytest tests/`, they need a postgres on localhost
- the release is made with `bump2version`, not with a manual edit of setup.py

A preference of the user goes to pending-memory.md first:

# Preferences waiting for a confirmation

- always answer in Chinese

and only lands in ~/.coderagent/CLAUDE.md after /memory confirm:

## Preferences

- always answer in Chinese

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text:
What you see What it means What to do The memory was not written: {path} would grow past 200 lines; tidy it up first. The file would become longer than 200 lines. Shorten the file, or split it. The reflection of the session failed (a warning in the log) The model did not answer with the expected JSON, so nothing was written. The session is not harmed. Nothing to do; the next turn tries again. Wrote 2 preference(s) to /Users/you/.coderagent/CLAUDE.md. The confirmation worked. — Nothing like that in the memory. /memory forget did not find the text. Check the text with /memory. Removed. /memory forget removed the text. —

The memory can be switched off entirely:

memory:
  enabled: false

docs.title: The extensions
docs.text:
• Sub agents — .coderagent/agents/*.md: a name, a description, a system prompt, a list of tools and a maximum number of turns. code-explorer, verifier and refactorer come with the agent. The model sees the index of them, so it can call them by name.
  • Skills — .coderagent/skills/<name>/SKILL.md: a package of steps, scripts and templates for a kind of task. The agent loads one when it fits.
  • Plugins — .coderagent/plugins: a Python module that adds tools, commands and hooks. A plugin has to be trusted once.
  • Hooks — six moments: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop and SessionEnd. A hook is a command that reads JSON and answers JSON: allow, deny or block, with a reason, with extra context or with rewritten arguments.
  • Your own commands — .coderagent/commands/*.md: a slash command with a description, an argument hint, the tools it may use and its own model.
  • MCP servers — a server over stdio. Its tools join the tools of the agent, they ask for permission like every other tool, and the connection is made again when it breaks.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A sub agent, .coderagent/agents/scout.md:

---
name: scout
description: Finds the place where a feature is implemented
tools: read, grep, glob, ls
model_purpose: cheap
max_turns: 15
---

You look for code. You never change anything. You answer with the files and
the line numbers.

The model calls it as a tool:

{"tool": "task", "params": {"subagent_type": "scout", "description": "where is the auth?", "prompt": "find the auth code"}}

and the answer is a JSON object:

{
  "status": "ok",
  "summary": "The auth is in src/auth/session.py.",
  "findings": ["src/auth/session.py:42 defines create_session"],
  "files_touched": [],
  "cost": 0.0004,
  "turns": 3,
  "purpose": "cheap"
}

A skill, .coderagent/skills/release/SKILL.md:

---
name: release
description: How to make a release of this project
---

1. Run the test suite.
2. Run `bump2version patch`.
3. Push the tag.

A hook, in the configuration:

hooks:
  events:
    PreToolUse:
      - matcher: "bash"
        hooks:
          - type: command
            command: ./.coderagent/hooks/check_secrets.sh
            timeout: 10
            strict: false

The hook reads JSON on stdin and answers JSON on stdout:

{"decision": "block", "reason": "the command writes a secret"}

decision is allow, deny or block; the hook may also add additionalContext or rewrite the call with updatedInput. For a tool the new input is a mapping of arguments; the UserPromptSubmit hook rewrites the prompt of the user with a string.

A custom command, .coderagent/commands/commit.md:

---
description: Make a commit of the changes
argument-hint: [message]
allowed-tools: bash, read
model: cheap
---

Commit everything with the message: $ARGUMENTS

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text:
What you see What it means What to do Error: unknown sub agent 'scout'. Available sub agents: code-explorer, refactorer, verifier. The name of the sub agent is not in the index. Use one of the listed names; the index of the custom ones is in the system prompt. Error: the sub agents are not available in this session. The task tool is not registered — tools.enabled was narrowed. Put task back into tools.enabled. Error: unknown skill 'release'. Available skills: {...}. The skill does not exist. The skills are .coderagent/skills/<name>/SKILL.md. Trusted 'x'. It is loaded the next time the agent starts. The answer of /plugins trust x. The plugin is used from the next session. Error: the hook blocked 'bash'. the command writes a secret A PreToolUse hook refused the call. Fix the command, or fix the hook. Hook 'check_secrets.sh' timed out, ignoring it The hook took longer than its timeout. The call goes through. Raise the timeout, or make the hook faster. Hook 'check_secrets.sh' failed with RuntimeError: ... The hook crashed. The call goes through. Fix the hook. With strict: true the call is blocked instead. Error: the MCP server 'echo' is not connected. The server is not running. Check the command of the server; /mcp says not connected or failed: <error>. Error: the MCP tool 'echo' failed: RuntimeError: ... The server answered with an error. The name in the message is the one of the server. The message of the server is in the answer.

The custom commands are looked up in <cwd>/.coderagent/commands/*.md only — the agent does not walk up the directories to find them.

docs.title: The sandbox
docs.text:
• Local by default — the commands run in the working directory.
  • Or in a container — docker, singularity, bubblewrap, contree, and the remote sandboxes of SWE-rex. The same environments as mini-swe-agent.
  • Only bash goes into the sandbox — the file tools stay in the working directory.
  • /sandbox — says where the commands run.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
sandbox:
  type: swerex_docker
  image: python:3.11

The seven types are local, docker, singularity, bubblewrap, contree, swerex_docker and swerex_modal. The options that the environment does not know are ignored, so one file can carry the settings of several of them.

/sandbox answers with the type, the options that are in effect and the environment that is in use:

type: local
environment: local

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text: What you see What it means What to do ValueError: Unknown environment type: nope (resolved to nope, available: {...}) The type is not one of the seven. Use one of the names above. CalledProcessError: Command '[...]' returned non-zero exit status 1. The container could not be started, or the image could not be pulled. Check the image name and that docker runs. FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'singularity' The binary of the environment is not installed. Install it, or use another type. The file tools touch the files of the host Only bash goes into the sandbox. That is by design: read, edit and friends work on the working directory of the session.

docs.title: The verification
docs.text:
• Off by default — nothing is checked unless verify.commands is set.
  • The agent has to make the check pass — when the model wants to stop, the commands run; if one of them fails, the agent gets the output and tries again.
  • The commands run in the session — in the sandbox when there is one, so the check sees the same world the agent works in. They do not ask for approval.
  • A bounded number of rounds — verify.max_rounds (3 by default). When the rounds are used up, the turn ends with stop_reason: verify_failed.
  • The result is in the log — an event of the type verify holds the commands and the ones that did not pass.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
verify:
  commands:
    - python -m pytest -q
  max_rounds: 3
  timeout: 300

When the model says it is done and the tests do not pass, the agent gets this back and keeps working:

[verify] These commands did not pass. Fix the problem and try again.

$ python -m pytest -q
2 failed, 1 passed
[exit code 1]

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text: What you see What it means What to do The turn ends with stop_reason: verify_failed The commands still failed after verify.max_rounds rounds. Read the output of the last round in the event log. The check runs in the sandbox and cannot find the files The sandbox does not have the working directory of the session. Give the environment a working directory, or use local. The check takes too long The command was killed after verify.timeout seconds. Raise verify.timeout. The agent keeps fixing the same thing The check needs something the agent cannot do. Fix the check or the task.

docs.title: The terminal interface
docs.text:
• The answer streams in — the text and the reasoning.
  • The status bar — the model, the tokens, the cost, the directory and the permission mode.
  • The tool cards — the call, the output and the diff of the change.
  • The approval — y, n and a, or the arrow keys on a numbered list.
  • Long output is folded away — the interesting part stays visible.
  • The todo panel — the task list of the current work.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
The status bar looks like this:

deepseek/deepseek-flash | 1.5k/64k | $0.0000 | ~/work/project | default

An approval is a numbered list, and the selected one is marked:

1 [*] y allow
2 [-] n deny
3 [-] a always allow

←/→ move the cursor, ↑/↓ do the same, the digits jump to a line, the space toggles a multiple choice, enter confirms, and y, n and a answer directly. ctrl+c interrupts the turn, ctrl+q settles the session and quits.

The todo panel marks the state of a task with ◉ (completed), ◐ (in progress) and ○ (pending).

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text: What you see What it means What to do Nothing happens when a tool wants approval The terminal is not there — the run is headless. The call is denied. Use --permission-mode bypass or a rule. ▸ 42 more lines under the output of a tool The output was longer than the card. The interesting part is visible; open the file, or run the command again with less output. The interface does not start coder without a task in a terminal starts the interface; without a terminal it prints no task given. Use coder --tui to force it.

docs.title: The web interface
docs.text:
• The chat page — three columns: the sessions and the files on the left, the conversation in the middle, the status, the changes and the file on the right.
  • The answer streams in — over a server sent event stream, and a browser that comes late reads the whole answer.
  • The settings page — the model as a form, the layer every field comes from, the preview of all the layers with the secrets taken out.
  • Test the connection — one cheap call, and it says whether the model calls the tools at all.
  • Test a model — a panel for an endpoint, a key and a model name, without writing anything.
  • The permissions in two places — the settings page for the next session, the chat page for the session that is running, right away.
  • The approvals in the browser — the same three answers.
  • The languages — English and Chinese. The switch in the top bar changes the whole page without a reload, and the choice is remembered in the browser and in a cookie. The region of the address decides when the visitor has not chosen.
  • The security model — no authentication, 127.0.0.1 by default, a header that a cross site request cannot send, a path that cannot leave the working directory, and a key that is only shown when it is asked for.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
coder web --cwd . --port 8765

coder web: http://127.0.0.1:8765

The API is plain HTTP. A message to a session:

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/sessions/20261109-3f0a91/messages \
  -H 'X-Coder-Client: 1' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text": "run the tests"}'

The stream of the events of a session:

curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/sessions/20261109-3f0a91/stream

The endpoints of the API:

Endpoint What it does GET /api/sessions The sessions of the working directory POST /api/sessions A new session GET /api/sessions/{id} One session GET /api/sessions/{id}/events The events of the session GET /api/sessions/{id}/items The items of the session after a sequence number GET /api/sessions/{id}/stream The stream of the events (SSE) GET /api/sessions/{id}/status The state, the model, the tokens, the cost GET /api/sessions/{id}/metrics The metrics of the session GET /api/sessions/{id}/changes The files that were changed POST /api/sessions/{id}/resume Continue the session POST /api/sessions/{id}/fork A copy of the session POST /api/sessions/{id}/messages Send a message POST /api/sessions/{id}/interrupt Interrupt the turn POST /api/sessions/{id}/mode Change the permission mode of the session POST /api/approvals/{id} Answer an approval GET /api/commands The slash commands GET /api/config The configuration and its layers PUT /api/config/model Write the model to the user level file GET /api/config/model/key The key of the endpoint PUT /api/config/permissions Write the permissions to the user level file POST /api/config/model/test One cheap call to test the model GET /api/files The files of the working directory GET /api/file One file GET /api/diff The diff of one file GET /api/i18n/{language} The strings of a language

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text:
Status Message What it means What to do 403 the X-Coder-Client header is missing A write without the header. A browser on another site cannot send it. Add -H 'X-Coder-Client: 1'. 404 there is no session with the id {id} The id is unknown. GET /api/sessions for the list. 404 no approval is waiting for the id {id} The approval was answered already, or it timed out. Nothing to do. 404 unknown language The language of /api/i18n/{language} is not one of the ones that are on. Use en or zh. 400 the message is empty The message has no text. Send a text. 400 unknown permission mode '{value}' The mode is not one of the five. Use default, acceptEdits, plan, readonly or bypass. 400 the decision must be allow, deny or always The answer of an approval is wrong. Use allow, deny or always. 400 '{path}' is not a directory A path of the file API is a file. Use a directory. 403 '{path}' is outside the working directory {cwd} The path leaves the working directory. Nothing — that is the boundary. 409 the session {id} is running The session is busy, so it cannot be forked or resumed. Wait for the turn to end, or interrupt it.

The approval that nobody answered is denied after ui.approval_timeout seconds, and the browser is told timed_out: true.

An approval of a tool that changes a file writes a rule into ~/.coderagent/rules.yaml — the same file the terminal uses.

The address of the server is printed on the start. With --host 0.0.0.0 the server warns:

The web interface listens on 0.0.0.0: everybody who can reach that address can drive the agent.

docs.title: The configuration
docs.text:
• Four layers — the defaults of the package, the project file .coderagent/config.yaml, the user file ~/.coderagent/config.yaml, and the overrides of the command line (-c key=value). The later wins.
  • The sections — model, agent, tools, permissions, context, memory, checkpoint, mcp, hooks, ui, sandbox and verify.
  • The paths — MSWEA_CODER_HOME moves the user level files somewhere else.
  • The settings page writes the user file only — the project file is in the repository and is never written.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# A file.
coder -t "..." -c myconf.yaml
# Overrides, repeatable.
coder -t "..." -c model.model_name=deepseek/deepseek-chat -c agent.max_turns=20

The layers, from the lowest to the highest priority:

  1. the defaults of the package (src/coderagent/config/defaults.yaml),
  2. .coderagent/config.yaml of the project,
  3. ~/.coderagent/config.yaml of the user,
  4. the -c of the command line.

The model name is looked up in this order: the -c of the command line, the project file, the user file, $MSWEA_MODEL_NAME, and at the end anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5.

The sections and what they hold:

Section The keys model model_name, model_kwargs, max_retries, litellm_config, routing, routing_rules, set_cache_control agent system_prompt, max_turns, cost_limit, token_limit, subagent_max_turns, subagent_max_parallel tools enabled, disabled, bash_timeout, max_output_tokens, schema_budget_tokens permissions mode, rules, deny_paths, include_dirs context context_window, reserved_output, compact_threshold, keep_recent_turns, keep_recent_token_ratio, compact_every_turns, auto_compact, summarize_model, summary_chunk_tokens memory project_path, user_path, enabled checkpoint enabled, keep mcp servers, timeout hooks events ui theme, show_reasoning, approval_timeout sandbox type and the options of the environment verify commands, max_rounds, timeout

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text: What you see What it means What to do Nothing happens, the setting is ignored A key that does not exist is ignored, silently. Check the spelling against the table above. yaml.scanner.ScannerError The YAML of a layer cannot be parsed. Fix the YAML; the message has the line. pydantic_core.ValidationError A value has the wrong type — a string where a number belongs. The message names the field. FileNotFoundError: Could not find config file for ... (tried: [...]) -c myconf.yml was given, but the file that is looked for is myconf.yaml. Use the name with .yaml, or give the full path. The model is not the one in the file A layer above the file wins. Remember the order; --list of the layers is on the settings page. ui.show_reasoning has no effect The key exists, but nothing reads it yet. The reasoning of the model is always shown in the terminal.

docs.title: The commands
docs.text:
Twenty-five built-in commands: /help, /model, /mode, /plan, /compact, /clear, /resume, /fork, /rewind, /diff, /init, /cost, /todos, /mcp, /permissions, /hooks, /agents, /skills, /plugins, /memory, /status, /sandbox, /export, /context and /exit (also /quit).

Your own commands live in .coderagent/commands/*.md and join them.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
coder -t "/cost"          # a command in the terminal
coder -t "/model deepseek/deepseek-chat"
coder -t "/mode plan"

A command that takes arguments is the rest of the line:

/model deepseek/deepseek-chat
/rewind 20261109-3f0a91

In the browser the commands are in the palette of the chat page, and the list comes from GET /api/commands.

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text: What you see What it means What to do Unknown command '/foo'. Try /help. There is no such command. /help lists them; /help <name> explains one. Unknown mode 'bogus'. Use one of: default, acceptEdits, plan, bypass, readonly. /mode was given a mode that does not exist. The mode of the session is unchanged. Use one of the five. /rewind with an id that is not a checkpoint ValueError: no checkpoint '<id>' in this session /rewind without an id lists the checkpoints. Not a git repository: {cwd} /diff runs git diff, and this directory is not a repository. Run it in a repository, or use the changes of the web page. {path} already exists. /init does not overwrite an AGENTS.md. Edit the file yourself. No sessions yet. /resume without an id found nothing in this directory. Run a turn first.

docs.title: The benchmark part of mini-swe-agent
docs.text:
• mini — a run script: a task, a model, an environment, and a trajectory file.
  • SWE-bench — the whole dataset, in parallel, with a slice and a filter.
  • SWE-bench, one instance — for a single problem.
  • ProgramBench — the programming benchmark.
  • The inspector — reads a trajectory file and shows what the agent did.
  • The environments — local, docker, singularity, bubblewrap, contree, SWE-rex docker and SWE-rex modal.
  • The models — litellm for most providers, and portkey, openrouter, requesty, the text based models and the roulette model besides.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
mini --model litellm/deepseek/deepseek-flash --environment-class docker \
  --task "the failing test is in test_api.py"

mini-extra swebench --model litellm/deepseek/deepseek-flash --workers 8 \
  --slice 0:100

The trajectory of a run is a JSON file with the messages, the tool calls and the cost of every step; inspector reads it.

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text: What you see What it means What to do The environment cannot be built The image is missing or the binary of the environment is not installed. The same errors as the sandbox of the coding agent. The model answers without a tool call The model of the benchmark is a text based one, or the format of the answer is wrong. Use a model that speaks the tool protocol, or a model class of the benchmark that wraps it.

docs.title: coding agent 的功能
docs.text:
coder 有什么本事，一条一条写下来。每一节最后都给出讲得更细的文档，每一节 都有用法例子和出错时怎么办。

English: The features of the coding agent

docs.title: 怎么用
docs.text:
• 终端里跑一轮——coder -t "把失败的测试修好"。结果按文本打印， 加 --output-format json 就是 JSON。
  • 终端界面——不给任务就是 coder，也可以 coder --tui。全屏界面， 有状态栏、工具卡片和审批。
  • 浏览器里——coder web。同一个 agent，一个聊天页，一个设置模型配置 的设置页。
  • 当 API 用——浏览器做的每个动作都是普通 HTTP 调用，脚本也能驱动它。
  • 当库用——coderagent.run.run_turn 和 build_loop 把 agent 放进别的 Python 程序里。
  • 跑 benchmark——mini-swe-agent 的那些运行脚本用同一套模型接口解 SWE-bench 和 ProgramBench。

docs.title: 用法例子
docs.text:
# 跑一轮，答案是文本。
coder -t "给 src/app.py 加个 docstring"

# 跑一轮，答案是 JSON（给脚本用）。
coder -t "列一下这个目录里的文件" --output-format json

# 终端界面。
coder                      # 在终端里这就是 TUI
coder --tui                # 明确写出来

# 浏览器。
coder web --cwd . --port 8765

# 这个目录的会话，最新的在前。
coder --list

一轮的 JSON 有这些字段：session_id、messages、cost、session_cost、 stop_reason、error。

{
  "session_id": "20261109-3f0a91",
  "messages": [{"role": "assistant", "content": "我把 docstring 加上了。"}],
  "cost": 0.0012,
  "session_cost": 0.0143,
  "stop_reason": "end_turn",
  "error": ""
}

cost 是这一轮花了多少，session_cost 是整个会话到目前为止花了多少。

stop_reason 是 end_turn、max_turns、cost_exceeded、token_limit、verify_failed、error、 interrupted 之一。

docs.title: 出错时怎么办
docs.text:
你看到的 什么意思 怎么办 no task given 没有 -t，也没有 --tui，而且 stdin 不是终端（脚本、管道）。 给个任务：coder -t "..."。 session 20261109-3f0a91 同上，但找到了可以续上的会话。 一样，加上 -t 就在里面跑一轮。 Unknown command '/foo'. Try /help. 这一行以 / 开头，但没有这个命令。 检查拼写，或者 /help 看列表。 ValueError: 'bogus' is not a valid PermissionMode --permission-mode bogus——这个值在建立权限策略时才检查，异常没有被捕获。 用 default、acceptEdits、plan、readonly、bypass 之一。 ValueError: Unknown output format: xml --output-format 只认 text 和 json。 用 text 或 json。 Unknown format 'xml'. Use json or otel. coder export --format 只认 json 和 otel。 用 json 或 otel。 no sessions yet --list 在这个目录里没找到会话。 不用管，先跑一轮。 stderr 上的 coder web: cannot listen on 127.0.0.1:8765 (Address already in use).，退出码 1 端口被占。服务启动前自己先探一下，因为 uvicorn 自己的报错不告诉你该怎么办。 换一个端口：coder web --port 8766。

正常跑完一轮 coder 的退出码是 0，不管答案是什么；连启动都没成功时 （标志的值不对、端口被占）是 1。

docs.title: 模型
docs.text:
• litellm 认识的任何厂商——OpenAI、DeepSeek、Anthropic、Gemini、 Mistral、OpenRouter……名字前面那个厂商决定调谁：deepseek/deepseek-flash。
  • 第三方端点——api_base 里写一个 OpenAI 兼容的地址，配它自己的 key。 地址可以直接粘完整的 /chat/completions，/v1 后面那段会被剪掉， 因为 litellm 自己会加。
  • 别名——一个带模型列表的 litellm 配置文件。模型名可以是那个列表里的 一条别名，端点的 key 就留在那个文件里。
  • 缓存标记——set_cache_control: default_end，给支持它的厂商用。别的值会被拒。
  • 重试——max_retries，默认三次。
  • 按用途路由——main、cheap、summarize、reflect、strong 可以 各配一个模型。
  • 按会话状态路由——像 tokens > 50000 这样的规则会换模型，理由写在 事件日志里。
  • 摘要用别的模型——context.summarize_model，留空就是 agent 自己那个。
  • 流式输出——答案一段一段到，终端和浏览器都是。

docs.title: 用法例子
docs.text:
# 厂商就是斜杠前面那段。
coder -t "..." -m deepseek/deepseek-flash

# 一个说 OpenAI 协议的第三方端点。
coder -t "..." -m openai/MiniMax-M2.7 \
  -c model.model_kwargs.api_base=https://api.example.com/v1 \
  -c model.model_kwargs.api_key=sk-...

# .coderagent/config.yaml
model:
  model_name: deepseek/deepseek-flash
  set_cache_control: default_end
  routing:
    main: deepseek/deepseek-chat
    cheap: deepseek/deepseek-flash
    summarize: deepseek/deepseek-flash
  routing_rules:
    - when: "tokens > 50000"
      purpose: strong

一轮用哪个模型，按这个顺序定：

  1. 用户用 /model 选的模型（它压过所有别的东西），
  2. 第一条成立的 routing_rules，
  3. 自动策略：预算快用完了 → cheap，上下文太大（超过 50000 token）或 会话太长（超过 30 轮）→ strong，
  4. routing.main，没有它就是 agent 自己的模型。

换了模型，事件日志里会写理由：

Switched from deepseek/deepseek-flash to deepseek/deepseek-chat: the context has grown

理由有这些：the budget is nearly used up、the context has grown、 the session has many turns、the rule '<when>' holds、 the rules of the routing say so。

docs.title: 出错时怎么办
docs.text:
你看到的 什么意思 怎么办 LLM Provider NOT provided 模型名前面没有厂商。 OpenAI 兼容的端点写 openai/<名字>，或者 deepseek/<名字>。 ValueError: Invalid mode: {mode} set_cache_control 既不是 default_end，也不是空的。 用 default_end，或者删掉这一行。 the file does not exist model.litellm_config 指的文件不在。 改路径，它是相对于工作目录的。 the file is not valid YAML: {error} 别名文件解析不了。 修 YAML。 the file has no model_list 别名文件里没有 model_list。 加上模型列表和它们的 litellm_params。 '{name}' is not one of the aliases of this file 模型名不在这个文件的 model_list 里。 用列表里的别名，或者去掉 litellm_config。 BadRequestError 厂商拒绝了请求（key 不对、名字不对、参数不对）。 不会重试，厂商的报错就是答案。 AuthenticationError key 缺了或者不对。 设 model.model_kwargs.api_key，或者在别名文件里写端点的 key，或者在环境里放厂商的 key（openai/… 找 OPENAI_API_KEY）。 ContextWindowExceededError 请求比模型的窗口大。 调小 context.context_window，或者换一个窗口更大的模型。

重试和上面的错误是两回事：限流和超时才重试，坏请求不重试。重试次数来自 MSWEA_MODEL_RETRY_STOP_AFTER_ATTEMPT，默认是 10。coder web 会用 model.max_retries（默认 3）去设这个变量，所以在浏览器里重试次数跟着配置 走，在终端里不跟。

docs.title: 工具
docs.text:
十三个内置工具：
